vocabulary.meaning_en: the things you usually do in the evening

vocabulary.meaning_en: to look at programmes on television

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make your clothes ready for the next day

vocabulary.meaning_en: things a family does together

vocabulary.meaning_en: making food with other people

vocabulary.meaning_en: making a place clean with other people

vocabulary.meaning_en: to read so that others can hear

vocabulary.meaning_en: to make an unhappy or worried face

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak very quietly

vocabulary.meaning_en: to act as if something is true when it is not

vocabulary.meaning_en: one of the soft light parts that cover a bird

vocabulary.meaning_en: the sound of someone walking

vocabulary.meaning_en: to become wider

vocabulary.meaning_en: delaying things you should do
vocabulary.example: Procrastination is a student's biggest enemy.
vocabulary.note_en: The verb is "procrastinate".

fine_lines.title: every day vs everyday
fine_lines.explanation_ar: تُنطقان بنفس الطريقة لكن تختلفان في الكتابة والوظيفة. every day (كلمتان) عبارة ظرفية معناها «كل يوم» وتجيب عن سؤال how often؟ أما everyday (كلمة واحدة) فهي صفة معناها «يومي / عادي / روتيني» ويجب أن يأتي بعدها اسم تصفه.

examples.sentence: I wash my face every day.
She goes to work every day.
Cleaning together is an everyday activity for us.

fine_lines.explanation_en: They sound the same but are written differently and do different jobs. "Every day" (two words) means "each day" and answers the question "how often?". "Everyday" (one word) is an adjective meaning "normal, ordinary, routine", and it must come before a noun.

fine_lines.title: nap vs doze off vs snooze
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الثلاثة لها علاقة بالنوم الخفيف أو القصير. nap قيلولة مقصودة ومخطط لها غالباً في النهار. doze off أن يغلبك النوم رغماً عنك دون تخطيط، مثلاً أمام التلفاز أو في المواصلات. snooze غفوة قصيرة جداً، وأشهر استخدام لها زر snooze في المنبّه لتسرق دقائق إضافية من النوم.

examples.sentence: I usually take a short nap after lunch.
Omar dozed off during the movie.
I hit the snooze button three times this morning.

fine_lines.explanation_en: All three are about light or short sleep. A "nap" is a planned short sleep, usually during the day. To "doze off" is to fall asleep without planning to, for example in front of the TV or on a bus. To "snooze" is to sleep for a very short time; it's best known from the snooze button on an alarm clock, which gives you a few extra minutes of sleep.

fine_lines.title: take a shower vs have a shower
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى واحد: يستحم. take a shower هي الأشيع في الإنجليزية الأمريكية، و have a shower أشيع في الإنجليزية البريطانية. ويمكن أيضاً استخدام shower وحدها كفعل: I need to shower.

examples.sentence: I take a shower every morning.
He's having a shower right now.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean to wash your body under a shower. "Take a shower" is more common in American English, and "have a shower" is more common in British English. You can also use "shower" alone as a verb: I need to shower.

fine_lines.title: do the dishes vs do the washing-up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلاهما بمعنى غسل الأطباق. wash the dishes أو do the dishes أمريكية وهي الأشهر عالمياً، و do the washing-up تعبير بريطاني شائع.

examples.sentence: It's your turn to do the dishes.
I'll do the washing-up after dinner.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean washing the plates after a meal. "Wash the dishes" or "do the dishes" is American and the most common around the world; "do the washing-up" is a common British expression.

grammar.title: Future continuous: an action in progress at a future time
grammar.explanation_ar: التركيب: will be + الفعل مع ing. نستخدمه لحدث سيكون جارياً ومستمراً في لحظة محددة في المستقبل. إذا ذكرنا وقتاً دقيقاً وسنكون في منتصف الحدث وقتها، نستخدم will be doing وليس will do.
examples: At 8 p.m. tomorrow, I'll be watching the match.
I can't meet you tomorrow morning. I'll be sitting in a lecture.
At 9 p.m. tonight, I will be doing my homework.
grammar.explanation_en: Form: will be + verb-ing. We use it for an action that will be in progress at a particular moment in the future. If we give an exact time and we will be in the middle of the action then, we use "will be doing", not "will do".

grammar.title: Future continuous for polite questions about plans
grammar.explanation_ar: سؤال Will you wash the dishes? بالمستقبل البسيط قد يبدو طلباً مباشراً أو أمراً. أما Will you be washing the dishes later? فهو سؤال لطيف عن خطط الشخص ونيّته دون ضغط عليه، لذلك يُعدّ أكثر تهذيباً.
examples: Will you be washing the dishes later?
Will you be using the car tonight?
Will you be going to the shop this afternoon?
grammar.explanation_en: "Will you wash the dishes?" (future simple) can sound like a direct request or an order. "Will you be washing the dishes later?" is a gentle question about the person's plans, with no pressure, so it sounds more polite.

questions.question: "These are my ___ shoes." (normal shoes I wear daily)
questions.explanation_ar: everyday كلمة واحدة صفة تصف الاسم shoes.
questions.explanation_en: "Everyday" (one word) is an adjective that describes the noun "shoes".

questions.question: "I go to the gym ___."
questions.explanation_ar: every day كلمتان بمعنى كل يوم وتدل على التكرار.
questions.explanation_en: "Every day" (two words) means each day and shows how often.

questions.question: At 9 p.m. tonight, I ___ my homework.
questions.explanation_ar: وقت محدد في المستقبل والحدث مستمر فيه، إذن المستقبل المستمر will be doing.
questions.explanation_en: A specific future time with an action in progress uses the future continuous: will be doing.

questions.question: Which question is the most polite way to ask about someone's plans?
choices: Will you be washing the dishes later?
questions.explanation_ar: المستقبل المستمر يسأل عن الخطة بلطف دون طلب مباشر.
questions.explanation_en: The future continuous asks about plans politely, without a direct request.

questions.question: He fell asleep in front of the TV without planning to. He ___.
questions.explanation_ar: doze off = يغفو رغماً عنه دون تخطيط.
questions.explanation_en: "Doze off" means to fall asleep without planning to.

questions.question: A short planned sleep during the day is a:
questions.explanation_en: A nap is a planned short sleep during the day.

questions.question: "To burn the midnight oil" means to:
choices: work or study late into the night
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير يعني السهر لوقت متأخر للعمل أو المذاكرة.
questions.explanation_en: It means staying up late to work or study.

questions.question: In British English, people usually say "___ a shower".
questions.explanation_ar: البريطانيون يقولون have a shower والأمريكيون take a shower.
questions.explanation_en: British people say "have a shower"; Americans say "take a shower".

questions.question: "Errands" are:

questions.question: The opposite of "occupied" (a room, a seat) is:
questions.explanation_ar: occupied = مشغول أو مأهول، وعكسها vacant = فارغ.
questions.explanation_en: "Occupied" means in use; the opposite is "vacant" (empty).
